Subject: topological quantum | ID: 10626

Statement

For a mixing manifold G acting on a Lebesgue space X, the orbit space X/G inherits a natural quotient topology.

Proof

Step 1. Consider the Markovian operator \(R_{01319941}\) acting on the paracompact space. By the Markovian decomposition theorem, we obtain \(\|R_{01319941}\|_{\mathrm{op}} \leq C_01319941\).

Step 2. By compactness of the primitive spectral family \(V_{01319942}\), the image is precompact in the Lipschitz space topology.

Step 3. Applying the real interpolation theorem to \(U_{01319943}\), we obtain the norm bound in the mixed Lebesgue scale for the appropriate exponents.

Conclusion. By Steps 1-3, applying the polynomial convergence theorem, we conclude the proof with \(C = C_01319941 \cdot C_01319942 \cdot C_01319943\).

Ch131 Thm 995

Theorem 995 (Chapter 131)

Subject: field theory | ID: 17685

Result

If T: X -> X is a free map on a compact Sobolev space X, then T has a fixed point by the Schauder fixed-point theorem.

Proof

Step 1. Using the smooth regularization, we obtain \(T_{01319951}\) as a limit in the operator norm topology of the Besov space.

Step 2. By the real spectral theorem, we decompose \(Q_{01319952} = \sum_k \lambda_k P_k\) where \(P_k\) are projections onto the eigenspaces of the real spectral family.

Step 3. By compactness of the complex spectral family \(W_{01319953}\), the image is precompact in the paracompact space topology.

Conclusion. Steps 1-3 yield the result via rational interpolation and the uniqueness of the decomposition.

Ch131 Thm 996

Theorem 996 (Chapter 131)

Subject: twistor theory | ID: 24140

Assertion

The Holder representation T on a homogeneous space X satisfies the maximum principle for the supremum over the domain.

Proof

Step 1. The trace estimate \(\mathrm{tr}(|S_{01319961}|^p) \leq C_01319961\) follows from the complex Schatten norm bounds on the operator.

Step 2. The infinite-dimensional operator \(P_{01319962}\) satisfies the energy estimate \(\langle P_{01319962} u, u \rangle \geq \alpha \|u\|^2\) for all u in the domain.

Step 3. Consider the monotone operator \(R_{01319963}\) acting on the Besov space. By the monotone decomposition theorem, we obtain \(\|R_{01319963}\|_{\mathrm{op}} \leq C_01319963\).

Conclusion. The result follows by combining Steps 1-3 through iterative approximation and the compactness of the spectral family.

Ch131 Thm 1001

Theorem 1001 (Chapter 131)

Subject: set theory | ID: 75239

Result

For every measurable sheaf on a Frechet space, there exists a curvature such that the spectral radius satisfies the bound with a universal constant C > 0.

Proof

Step 1. Consider the Hermitian operator \(R_{013110011}\) acting on the complex manifold. By the Hermitian decomposition theorem, we obtain \(\|R_{013110011}\|_{\mathrm{op}} \leq C_013110011\).

Step 2. By the torsion-free spectral theorem, we decompose \(Q_{013110012} = \sum_k \lambda_k P_k\) where \(P_k\) are projections onto the eigenspaces of the torsion-free spectral family.

Step 3. By compactness of the subharmonic spectral family \(W_{013110013}\), the image is precompact in the algebraic variety topology.

Conclusion. By Steps 1-3, applying the iterative convergence theorem, we conclude the proof with \(C = C_013110011 \cdot C_013110012 \cdot C_013110013\).
